questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: At night.
When it is raining.
Both of the above

questions.explanation: In good conditions, keep a four-second distance between you and the car ahead. In darkness or bad weather, increase this distance.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Develop a habit before driving. Buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs before you start the car.

questions.question: If your car has airbags, what else should you use?

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags protect you during a crash. For the best protection, always wear your seat belt along with airbags.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It reduces your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions affect how well you drive. If you are worried, excited, scared, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress makes it hard to concentrate on driving. Wait to drive until you feel calm.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, or swerve across lanes on the highway. Do not cross the median to turn around. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.explanation: Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your body. Drinking coffee or taking a shower will not help.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal when you change lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal when you change lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all laws, signs, signals, and road markings. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for the conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions cause many accidents. Drive with the flow of traffic and within the speed limit.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing drivers.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Exit the road safely and park where other drivers can see you. Raise your hood to show your car is disabled.

questions.question: When must you report a crash to police?

options.text: Someone is hurt.
Damage is more than $1,000.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Report a crash to police if anyone is hurt or if damage is $1,000 or more (or $200 or more to government property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness and concentration, slows reaction time, and reduces coordination.

questions.question: What happens to drivers who drink alcohol before driving?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks they take.
They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.
They have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms judgment, vision, concentration, understanding of reality, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus turns.
Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.
questions.explanation: Never squeeze your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning before you turn.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention to change lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes to alert other drivers. Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns.
No outlet.
No U-turns.

questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You often see this sign at intersections with heavy oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Vehicles turning left on a green light must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles turning left on a green light must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.
questions.explanation: This sign works with a traffic signal to tell drivers that left-turning vehicles do not have the right-of-way. They must wait for oncoming traffic to clear.

questions.question: Your vehicle has a mechanical problem. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, other drivers need to see it. Get off the road if possible and turn on hazard lights to show you need help.

questions.question: Why should you not stop suddenly in front of large trucks or buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop and start than small vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle may cause a crash because the driver cannot stop in time.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is injured.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911. Report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms reaction time and vision. It also affects your judgment of speed and distance, lowers caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: Driving ability can be hurt by:

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Not getting enough sleep.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs (legal or illegal), and drowsiness can all impair your driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
Dangerous curve ahead.
Bump in the road ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They warn drivers of hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers to be careful when the road is wet because it may be slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both effects may become stronger.
Nothing will happen.
Both effects may become weaker.
Only the alcohol effect becomes weaker.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and another drug can strengthen the effects of both. For example, one drink plus a cold medicine might affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: When driving near trucks, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than cars.
Need less time to pass on a downhill than cars.
Have a smaller turning radius than cars.
Need less time to pass on an uphill than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than cars.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are heavier and larger, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: When you see an angry driver around you:

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't use hand gestures.
Stay away from them.
All of these.

questions.explanation: When another driver is angry, stay away from them. Avoid eye contact and hand gestures that could make them angrier. Slow down, move away, or do what you safely can to protect yourself.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Follow the car ahead too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To prevent aggressive driving, stay focused and calm. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Plan your travel time, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Slow down when you see this warning.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Entering or leaving a parking space.
Entering traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, entering or leaving a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals tell other drivers what you're doing and help prevent crashes.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:

options.text: Weaken the effects of both.
Strengthen the effects of both.
Help cure your illness.
Improve your driving.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can strengthen the effects of both. Driving after using either is unsafe. Combining them is even more dangerous.
